title: Pinning in the S&P 500 Futures
one_line: S&P 500 futures are pulled toward the at-the-money strike on days when serial options on the futures expire ('pinning'), and pushed away from it just before S&P 500 index options expire ('anti-cross-pinning'); the hedging-driven shift is at least $115 million notional per expiration.

findings.statement: Pinning toward the nearest strike on futures-option expiration days.
Mechanism: delta-hedge rebalancing by market makers as hedges decay, and retail reselling of in-the-money options.

why.pattern: Dealer delta-hedge decay into expiration pulls price toward heavily-held strikes.

reported_results.headline: S&P 500 futures are pulled toward the at-the-money strike on days when serial options on the futures expire ('pinning'), and pushed away from it just before S&P 500 index options expire ('anti-cross-pinning'); the hedging-driven shift is at least $115 million notional per expiration.

tradable_edge: New quick-screen spec expiration_pin_es: on monthly/weekly ES option expiration afternoons, does price close nearer a round strike (25-pt multiple) than on other days, and does a fade-toward-strike rule pay? Strike open interest is not available — round numbers are the proxy.
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project). Needs options positioning / open-interest data we do not have; ES/NQ price data only allows proxies.
